facts.statement: Alexandronectes was a long-necked marine reptile belonging to the elasmosaurid plesiosaur family.
facts.quote: Alexandronectes is a genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur, a type of long-necked marine reptile, that lived in the oceans of Late Cretaceous New Zealand.

facts.statement: The genus Alexandronectes contains only one known species, A. zealandiensis.
facts.quote: It contains one species, A. zealandiensis.

facts.statement: Fossils of Alexandronectes were discovered in the Conway Formation of Canterbury, dating to the Early Maastrichtian stage of the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Fossils of Alexandronectes were found in the Conway Formation of Canterbury, which can be dated to the Early Maastrichtian stage of the Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The fossils of Alexandronectes were discovered by Alexander McKay.
facts.quote: Fossils were found by Alexander McKay.

facts.statement: The holotype specimens are cataloged as M Zfr 73 and CM Zfr 91.
facts.quote: The specimen was cataloged as M Zfr 73 and CM Zfr 91.

facts.statement: The genus and species Alexandronectes zealandiensis were formally described in 2016 by Otero et al. in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.
facts.quote: In 2016 Otero, R. A., O'Gorman, J. P., Hiller, N., O'Keefe, F. R. & Fordyce, R. E. published in Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology a paper titled Alexandronectes zealandiensis gen. et sp. nov., a new aristonectine plesiosaur from the lower Maastrichtian of New Zealand, making a formal description of a new plesiosaur genus and species.

facts.statement: Alexandronectes is classified in the subfamily Aristonectinae based on its pterygoid structure and an A-shaped squamosal arch.
facts.quote: Alexandronectes belongs to the elasmosaurid subfamily Aristonectinae based on the pterygoid structure and an A-shaped squamosal arch.

facts.statement: Alexandronectes differs from other aristonectines by having a smaller skull, distinct paroccipital processes, and a different mandibular glenoid.
facts.quote: However, it differs from other aristonectines in its smaller skull, different paroccipital processes, and different mandibular glenoid.

facts.statement: Researchers classified Alexandronectes within the Elasmosauridae family and the Aristonectinae subfamily.
facts.quote: Researchers classified that animal in elasmosaurid family and Aristonectinae subfamily.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis suggests that Kaiwhekea is the closest relative of Alexandronectes.
facts.quote: It resulted in a strict consensus trees, according to which closest kin of Alexandronectes was Kaiwhekea.
